title: Unirational parametrization of a torus over an arbitrary field
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], and let $T$ be a $k$-torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type], that is, a $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] becoming $\mathbf G_m^r$ over an algebraic closure for some finite $r\geq0$. There exist an integer $n\geq0$, a nonempty open subscheme $U\subseteq\mathbb A^n_k$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-sbc-affine-space], and a $k$-morphism $q:U\to T$ whose image is Zariski dense in $T$. Here $\mathbb A^n_k=\operatorname{Spec}k[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; dense image means that every nonempty open subset of $T$ has nonempty inverse image under $q$. This includes the trivial torus and arbitrary imperfect or finite fields.

source.place: Definition 12.59 and its equivalent dominant-open parametrization, printed p.250; Proposition 12.64, printed p.251, using Propositions 12.60 and 12.63.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-torus-induced-quotient] to $T$. Obtain $m\geq1$, finite separable extensions $L_i/k$, $A=\prod_i L_i$, the affine torus $P$ representing $R\mapsto(A\otimes_kR)^\times$, and a homomorphism $\pi:P\to T$ surjective on scheme points. This uses no perfection or infinitude hypothesis on $k$.

source.place: Proposition 12.63, printed p.251, with Lemma 12.61 and Definition 12.62. The displayed product of restrictions has the stated unit functor. A redundant factor L=k allows m>=1, also for the trivial torus.

proof.text: Choose a finite $k$-basis $e_1,\ldots,e_d$ of $A$: concatenate bases of the finitely many finite-dimensional fields, placing each basis vector in its own component. The product is nonzero because $m\geq1$, so $d\geq1$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-algebra-units-affine-chart] to this basis and to the representing affine scheme $P$ from step 1. It gives a nonempty principal open $U=D(N)\subseteq\mathbb A^d_k$ and an isomorphism $\theta:U\xrightarrow{\sim}P$. In particular the coordinates of $1_A$ lie in $U$ because their determinant is $1$.

source.place: Proposition 12.60, proof, printed p.250: basis coordinates and norm polynomial. The identical multiplication-matrix construction applies to any finite-dimensional commutative algebra. For arbitrary test algebras R, read norm invertible, rather than merely nonzero (see report Source error).

proof.text: Set $n=d$ and $q=\pi\circ\theta:U\to T$. For every scheme point $t$ of $T$, surjectivity of $\pi$ supplies $p\in P$ with $\pi(p)=t$; the inverse isomorphism $\theta^{-1}$ supplies $u\in U$ with $q(u)=t$. Thus $q$ is surjective on scheme points, and every nonempty open $V\subseteq T$ has a point $t$ and hence a point in $q^{-1}(V)$. Its image is therefore dense as required. For the trivial torus one may take $L_1=k$, so this construction also covers rank zero without any claim about density of rational points over finite fields.

source.place: Proposition 12.64, printed p.251, combining 12.60 and 12.63; Definition 12.59, printed p.250.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 12.64 via Propositions 12.60 and 12.63, printed pp.250-251.

I tested A=k, A=k×k and A=k[ε]/ε² (N=x1², which matches the units of R[ε] for R with nilpotents).
